subproblem.title: Second-variation integrand of a normal variation: trace and Q identities
subproblem.statement:
Second-variation integrand of a normal variation (linear algebra). Data: P ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace S ⊆ ℝ^P; ν₀ ∈ ℝ^P; linear maps N, L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P and g : ℝ^P → ℝ; ζ ∈ ℝ. Hypotheses: |ν₀| = 1; ν₀·v = 0 for every v ∈ S; N(S) ⊆ S; η·Nτ = τ·Nη for all τ, η ∈ S; Lτ = g(τ)ν₀ + ζNτ for every τ ∈ S. Conclusion: trace(P_S∘L) = ζ·trace(P_S∘N), and
 Σ_{j=1}^P (|L(P_Se_j) − P_S L(P_Se_j)|² − P_Se_j·L(P_S L(P_Se_j))) = Σ_j g(P_Se_j)² − ζ²·Σ_j |N(P_Se_j)|²,
where P_S is the orthogonal projection onto S and e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ν₀ : Euclid P) (N L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (g : Euclid P →L[ℝ] ℝ) (ζ : ℝ), ‖ν₀‖ = 1 → (∀ v ∈ S, inner ℝ ν₀ v = 0) → (∀ τ ∈ S, N τ ∈ S) → (∀ τ ∈ S, ∀ η ∈ S, inner ℝ η (N τ) = inner ℝ τ (N η)) → (∀ τ ∈ S, L τ = g τ • ν₀ + ζ • N τ) → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (S.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ L.toLinearMap) = ζ * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (S.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ N.toLinearMap) ∧ ∑ j : Fin P, (‖L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) - S.starProjection (L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))‖ ^ 2 - inner ℝ (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) (L (S.starProjection (L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))))) = ∑ j : Fin P, (g (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))) ^ 2 - ζ ^ 2 * ∑ j : Fin P, ‖N (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1))‖ ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. The substitution step of parent (1c) ('Insert (1b), using (0.2)–(0.4)': a = 0, (DZτ)^⊥ = (Dζ̃τ)ν, Σ(τ_i·DZτ_j)(τ_j·DZτ_i) = ζ̃²|A|²), written without choosing a basis of S. No dependencies.

Notation. P := P_S, u_j := Pe_j ∈ S.

1. (Projection facts.) P is self-adjoint, Pw ∈ S for every w, Pw = w for w ∈ S (so P² = P), and Pν₀ = 0, because ν₀ ∈ S^⊥ (ν₀·v = 0 for v ∈ S; Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff).

2. (Trace in the standard basis.) For every linear R : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, trace(P∘R) = Σ_j u_j·Ru_j. Indeed P∘R = P∘(P∘R), hence trace(P∘R) = trace((P∘R)∘P) (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'); in the standard orthonormal basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun) this is Σ_j e_j·P(R(Pe_j)) = Σ_j Pe_j·R(Pe_j) (P self-adjoint).

3. (First claim.) For each j, u_j ∈ S, so Lu_j = g(u_j)ν₀ + ζNu_j and u_j·Lu_j = g(u_j)(u_j·ν₀) + ζ(u_j·Nu_j) = ζ(u_j·Nu_j). Summing over j and applying step 2 to R = L and to R = N gives trace(P∘L) = ζ·trace(P∘N).

4. (Normal component.) Nu_j ∈ S, so PNu_j = Nu_j and PLu_j = g(u_j)Pν₀ + ζPNu_j = ζNu_j. Hence Lu_j − PLu_j = g(u_j)ν₀ and |Lu_j − PLu_j|² = g(u_j)²|ν₀|² = g(u_j)².

5. (Tangential component.) Since Nu_j ∈ S, L(PLu_j) = ζL(Nu_j) = ζ(g(Nu_j)ν₀ + ζN(Nu_j)). Therefore u_j·L(PLu_j) = ζg(Nu_j)(u_j·ν₀) + ζ²(u_j·N(Nu_j)) = ζ²(Nu_j·Nu_j) = ζ²|Nu_j|², using ν₀ ⊥ S and the symmetry hypothesis with τ := Nu_j ∈ S and η := u_j ∈ S.

6. (Second claim.) Subtracting step 5 from step 4 and summing over j: Σ_j(|Lu_j − PLu_j|² − u_j·L(PLu_j)) = Σ_j g(u_j)² − ζ²Σ_j|Nu_j|². ∎
proof_key_steps: trace(P_S∘R) = trace(P_S∘R∘P_S) = Σ_j P_Se_j·R(P_Se_j) for every linear R.
On S: P_S L = ζN and (I − P_S)L = g(·)ν₀, since ν₀ ⊥ S and N(S) ⊆ S.
Symmetry of N on S gives P_Se_j·L(P_S L P_Se_j) = ζ²|N P_Se_j|²; sum over j.

audit.reason: Projection annihilates ν₀ and fixes N(S), giving the normal component and trace identity. Symmetry of N turns the remaining quadratic term into ζ²‖Nu_j‖². Both conclusions match the Lean proposition, including the scope of the two final sums.
